title: Sell the {good} now?
body: {agent} is home from {to} after {seasons}, and the {good} is in your store. A broker will take two loads today for 200 dinars, a little under the market. Or you can hold it and wait for news of prices.

choices.label: Sell two loads to the broker
choices.hint: You get 200 dinars now. Buyers remember a house that sells fast.

choices.label: Hold the {good} for news
choices.hint: It stays in your store. The price may rise or fall.

note: Pegolotti's handbook, written about 1340 for merchants, lists weights, duties and freight at many ports. A merchant could use such lists to work out what a price far away was really worth.

sources.at: the handbook as a whole; the Alexandria chapter, print p. 72, and freight, print p. 75

title: A bigger share for {agent}?
body: {agent} is home from {to} after {seasons}. The house made money, and {agent} kept a third under the qirad. {agent} hints that the road was hard.

choices.label: Offer {agent} a bigger share next time
choices.hint: {agent} will be glad. Your partners may grumble.

choices.label: Keep to one third
choices.hint: Partners like a house that keeps its terms.

note: In the Geniza contracts the traveller's share was normally one third. Other splits were found, and the split was a matter of the contract, not of law.

sources.at: pp. 317 and 325; the traveller's share, normally one third
the split of profit as a matter of contract, in the section on the commenda

title: A bonus for {agent}?
body: {agent} is home from {to} after {seasons}, and the house made money. A bonus is not in the contract. It would be a thank you.

choices.label: Pay {agent} a bonus of 30 dinars
choices.hint: It costs now. {agent} will remember it.

choices.label: Pay nothing more
choices.hint: The house keeps all of it.

note: In the Geniza papers a commission, a fee for one special job, was paid for that service and not for the friendship. A traveller who kept a share of the profit was paid by results.

sources.at: p. 316 for the commission paid for a special service; p. 317 for the share of the profit

title: Some goods were lost
body: {agent} is home from {to} after {seasons}, but some of the goods were lost on the road. Your partners put money in this trip. They will want to know.

choices.label: Tell the partners yourself
choices.hint: It is honest. {agent} may feel blamed.

choices.label: Say nothing until they ask
choices.hint: {agent} is grateful. Partners dislike hearing it late.

note: In one Geniza case a man lost almost 50 of the 70 dinars he sent overseas. His community's elders convinced him he had no claim.

sources.at: p. 325; the investor who lost almost fifty of seventy dinars

title: The trip lost money
body: {agent} is home from {to} after {seasons}, and the trip lost money. Under a qirad the loss is yours and your partners'. {agent} owes nothing for it, unless the terms were broken.

choices.label: Keep the qirad as it stands
choices.hint: {agent} is grateful. Other agents hear of it.

choices.label: Ask {agent} for an account of every sale
choices.hint: {agent} feels doubted. Partners are glad you checked.

note: In the Muslim commenda the traveller did not repay lost money, even if it was all of it. He paid only if he broke his orders or the customs of merchants.

sources.at: the loss in the commenda, in the section on its characteristics
p. 325; the traveller who bears no loss

title: The trip lost money
body: {agent} is home from {to} after {seasons}, and the trip lost money. {agent} says the road was bad luck, and not a fault. You paid {agent} a wage, so the loss is yours.

choices.label: Say it was a fair risk
choices.hint: {agent} is grateful. Other agents hear of it.

choices.label: Take 20 dinars from {agent}'s next pay
choices.hint: The house gets some back. {agent} will not forget it.

note: In one Geniza case a man lost almost 50 of the 70 dinars he sent overseas. His community's elders convinced him he had no claim.

sources.at: p. 325; the investor who lost almost fifty of seventy dinars

title: Out again, or rest?
body: {agent} is home from {to} after {seasons}. A partnership usually ran for a year and was renewed if both sides liked it. Will you send {agent} out again?

choices.label: Send {agent} out again
choices.hint: The next sheet shows what sending {agent} costs.

choices.label: Let {agent} rest a season
choices.hint: A rested agent is glad of it.

note: In the Geniza papers the standard period of a partnership was one year, and it was renewed if the partners wished. Where a venture ran longer, accounts were made every year.

sources.at: p. 326 for the standard year and its renewal; p. 327 for yearly accounts

title: A long way home
body: {agent} is home from {to} after {seasons}. That is a long time on the road. {agent} looks tired. A partnership usually ran for a year, and this one ran much longer.

choices.label: Send {agent} out again
choices.hint: The next sheet shows what sending {agent} costs.

choices.label: Let {agent} rest a season
choices.hint: A rested agent is glad of it. The house loses a season.

note: In the Geniza papers the standard period of a partnership was one year, and it was renewed if the partners wished. Where a venture ran longer, accounts were made every year.

sources.at: p. 326 for the standard year and its renewal; p. 327 for yearly accounts

title: {agent} did not come back
body: {agent} sailed for {to}, and the ship did not come in. No one has seen it since. Ships on the sea road were sometimes lost with all aboard.

choices.label: Help {agent}'s family
choices.hint: It costs now. The other agents hear of it.

choices.label: Ask the partners to share the loss
choices.hint: They may agree. They will not like being asked.

choices.label: Do nothing more
choices.hint: The agents hear of that too.

note: Ibn Battuta wrote of a junk that was driven ashore and broken in pieces. On the Malabar coast the goods of a wrecked ship went to the ruler. Only at Calicut did the owners keep them.

sources.at: vol. 4, pp. 815 to 816; the junk driven ashore and broken in pieces, and the custom of wrecks on the coast and at Calicut

title: {agent} is safe
body: The ship for {to} was lost, but {agent} came ashore alive. The goods are gone.

choices.label: Say it was no one's fault
choices.hint: {agent} is grateful.

choices.label: Blame {agent} for the loss
choices.hint: {agent} will not forget it.

title: {agent} did not come back
body: {agent} set out for {to} with the caravan, and it did not arrive. The road is long, and a caravan that misses its wells can be lost.

choices.label: Help {agent}'s family

choices.label: Ask the partners to share the loss
choices.hint: They may agree. They will not like being asked.

note: In Fatimid times the desert crossing from Aydhab to the Nile took 15 or 20 days. Al-Maqrizi wrote that Bedouin raided Aydhab. In the Sahara, Ibn Battuta wrote, it was ten days' travel beyond Taghaza with no water, or only rarely.

title: {agent} did not come back
body: {agent} took a boat for {to}, and the boat did not come in. The river was high, and the boatmen could not say where it was lost.

choices.label: Help {agent}'s family
choices.hint: It costs now. The other agents hear of it.

choices.label: Ask the partners to share the loss
choices.hint: They may agree. They will not like being asked.

choices.label: Do nothing more

note: No account of a lost Nile boat was reached, so this scene is invented. What is recorded is that boats loaded with crops, spices and sugar sailed in the flood. In July 1326 Ibn Battuta came down from Qus in eight nights.

vol. 1, p. 71; eight nights in the flood of July 1326

title: Robbers took some of the goods
body: Robbers took part of the load on the way to {to}. {agent} is safe and goes on. The rest of the goods are still with {agent}.

choices.label: Ask the officers to search
choices.hint: It costs now. The court may remember you asked.

choices.label: Ask {agent} for an account of the day
choices.hint: Your partners are glad you asked. {agent} feels doubted.

choices.label: Let it go
choices.hint: {agent} is grateful that you did not fuss.

note: Al-Maqrizi wrote of Bedouin raids on Aydhab, as the Peacocks tell it. In 1326 a war stopped Ibn Battuta there. The king of the Beja was fighting the sultan's soldiers.

sources.at: p. 38; raids by Bedouin on Aydhab, citing al-Maqrizi, and Ibn Battuta stopped by the fighting
